days.title: The great stones
days.summary: The day opens on Salisbury Plain at the most famous prehistoric monument in Europe, then the ceremonial Avenue and the builders' henge nearby.

stops.name: Stonehenge · the sarsen circle
stops.blurb: The most famous prehistoric monument in Europe — a ring of sarsen and bluestone raised on Salisbury Plain around 2500 BC and aligned to the solstice sun. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stops.name: The Avenue & Heel Stone
stops.blurb: The ceremonial approach the builders walked — a low earthwork running to the outlying Heel Stone, where the midsummer sun rises over the circle.

stops.name: Durrington Walls & Woodhenge
stops.blurb: A vast henge and the builders' village beside it — where the people who raised Stonehenge lived and feasted midwinter.

days.title: Ancient Wessex
days.summary: North onto the Marlborough Downs — the greatest stone circle in the world, Europe's tallest prehistoric mound, a tomb you can enter, and Britain's oldest hill figure.

stops.name: Avebury · the great circle
stops.blurb: The largest stone circle in the world — so vast a village sits inside it. Older and greater in span than Stonehenge, ringed by a huge Neolithic bank and ditch. UNESCO World Heritage.

stops.name: Silbury Hill
stops.blurb: The tallest prehistoric mound in Europe — 30 m of chalk raised by hand about 4,400 years ago, its purpose still unknown.

stops.name: West Kennet Long Barrow
stops.blurb: A 5,600-year-old chambered tomb you can still step inside — one of the largest and best-preserved Neolithic burial mounds in Britain.

stops.name: Uffington White Horse
stops.blurb: A 3,000-year-old chalk-cut horse streaming across the downs — the oldest hill figure in Britain, best read from the ridgeway above.

days.title: Cathedral city & the country house
days.summary: South to the old hillfort and the cathedral with Britain's tallest spire, then the golden-hour drive across Cranborne Chase to a Georgian country house for the night.

stops.name: Old Sarum
stops.blurb: The great Iron-Age hillfort that became the first Salisbury — ramparts, a ruined royal castle and the footings of the original cathedral.

stops.name: Salisbury Cathedral
stops.blurb: Britain's tallest spire at 123 m, and home to one of only four surviving 1215 originals of Magna Carta, in a cathedral close little changed in 800 years.

stops.name: Cranborne Chase · downland dusk
stops.blurb: A protected chalk landscape of ancient droves and fallow deer — the golden-hour run back, hares in the barley and red kites overhead.

stops.name: The Country House · your stay
stops.blurb: Where the day ends — a Georgian manor of mellow stone, log fires, a walled garden and a long candle-lit table. A generic composite, not a specific hotel.

stops.name: Slow country morning
stops.blurb: Breakfast in the orangery before you set out — local eggs, garden fruit and a pot of proper tea.
